hints: Count input values divisible by each candidate gcd.
All nonempty subsets of those values have gcd divisible by that candidate.
Process gcd values downward and subtract subsets with larger exact gcd.
analogy: Count all groups divisible by k, then remove groups already assigned a larger gcd.
example: For [2,4], exact gcd 2 occurs for subsets [2] and [2,4], while exact gcd 4 occurs for [4].
algorithm: Count frequencies of input values. For each k from n down to 1, sum frequencies at multiples of k; start with 2^count-1 modulo 10^9+7, then subtract the previously computed exact counts for all proper multiples of k. Print the resulting counts.
correctness: A subset has every element divisible by k exactly when its gcd is a multiple of k. The downward subtraction partitions these subsets by their unique exact gcd.
complexity: For n values bounded by n, O(n log n) time and O(n) space.
